angle: Agents create value only when scoped to real workflows with metrics, guardrails, and human handoffs.
sourceTitle: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything. Will everyone use them?
linkedinPost:
“An agent for everything” sounds great—until it tries to do everything at once inside your company.

TechCrunch reports on the push to bring AI agents from engineers to everyone. The promise is software that can take actions, not just draft answers. In the enterprise, that’s where the risk—and the value—both live.

My take from FDE work: agents don’t replace business processes; they amplify them. If your returns process is fuzzy, an agent will automate confusion faster. If your knowledge is scattered, it will confidently act on partial truths.

What works in production:
- Narrow missions (“close level-1 billing tickets within policy”), not open-ended assistants.
- Clear guardrails (systems of record it may touch, thresholds for human review).
- Telemetry and SLAs (cycle time, first-contact resolution, error budgets) tied to dollars.
- Designed handoffs to humans when confidence, cost, or ethics trip a rule.

Pilot for a week, but instrument for a quarter. The winners won’t have the flashiest demos—they’ll have the cleanest handoffs and clearest ROI.

Where would a tightly scoped agent actually move a KPI in your world? #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption #AIStrategy
